ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The structure in the figure is basically left-right symmetric, with an N=N azo double bond at the center. The left azo nitrogen is connected to a tertiary substituted carbon, and this carbon is also connected to two methyl groups and connected to a nitrile group labeled NC; the right azo nitrogen is connected to the corresponding tertiary substituted carbon, and this carbon is likewise connected to two methyl groups and a nitrile group labeled CN. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring them. Reasoning: The left half can be written as a tert-substituted carbon connected to two methyl groups, a nitrile group, and an azo nitrogen, namely CC(C)(C#N)N. The central connection is N=N. The right half is symmetric, as NC(C)(C)C#N attached to the other end of the double bond. Therefore the complete SMILES is CC(C)(C#N)N=NC(C)(C)C#N.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image? Ignore the arrows.

method.method_draft: Ignore all curved arrows. Parse the left half as a tert-substituted carbon attached to two methyl groups, one nitrile group, and the left azo nitrogen: CC(C)(C#N)N. Parse the center as an azo double bond N=N. Parse the right half symmetrically as the second azo nitrogen attached to C(C)(C)C#N. Concatenate these fragments respecting the N=N connection to obtain CC(C)(C#N)N=NC(C)(C)C#N.

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know that the requested output is the SMILES expression of the depicted transition-state structure and that arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply standard organic structure conventions: terminal CN/NC labels attached to carbon represent nitrile groups C#N; line ends are carbons with implicit hydrogens; a tetravalent branching carbon can be written in SMILES with parenthetical methyl and nitrile branches; an azo linkage is written N=N.
